859	/// Windows bitmap: `BM`, then a 14-byte BITMAPFILEHEADER, then a DIB header
860	/// that opens with its own size.
861	///
862	/// The discriminator is the DIB header size and the two fields immediately
863	/// behind it. Every DIB header ever defined is between 12 (BITMAPCOREHEADER)
864	/// and 124 (BITMAPV5HEADER) bytes, so its little-endian u32 puts three NUL
865	/// bytes at offsets 15..18, where `BMW,model,year` puts `ar\n`. Colour planes
866	/// is then fixed at 1 by every variant of the header, which pins a fourth NUL,
867	/// and bit depth behind it is a closed set. Those are the checks text cannot
868	/// pass; the pixel-array offset must additionally clear both headers.
869	///
870	/// Two tighter rules were tried first, in round 1 of #379, and both refuse real
871	/// bitmaps — which is the failure this table exists to prevent, so neither is
872	/// used:
873	///
874	///   * `bfReserved1/2` at offsets 6..10 are specified as zero, but a bitmap
875	///     converted from a CUR or ICO carries the cursor hot-spot coordinates
876	///     there.
877	///   * a closed set of DIB sizes `{12, 16, 40, 52, 56, 64, 108, 124}` admits
878	///     five of the OS/2 2.x BITMAPCOREHEADER2 sizes, which are legally anything
879	///     in `16..=64`, and refuses the other 44.
880	///
881	/// Only 3 real BMPs exist on the build machine, all BITMAPINFOHEADER with zero
882	/// reserved words, so unlike the GIF sweep this is reasoned from the format
883	/// definitions rather than measured against a corpus — but the mechanism is the
884	/// one that demonstrably broke GIF, and a synthetic hot-spot / OS/2 bitmap does
885	/// sniff `txt-prose` under the old rule. Pinned by
886	/// `real_bmp_shapes_the_closed_set_refused`.
887	///
888	/// `bfSize` (offsets 2..6) is deliberately NOT compared against the file
889	/// length, which is what #379 proposed. Two reasons, both structural: this
890	/// function classifies from the `read_prefix(path, gzip, 8192)` buffer and has
891	/// no file length to compare against, and for a gzipped member the on-disk
892	/// length is the *compressed* length, so the comparison would be wrong exactly
893	/// where it was applied.
894	fn bmp_file_header(prefix: &[u8]) -> bool {
895	    if prefix.len() < 18 {
896	        return false;
897	    }
898	    let pixel_offset = u32::from_le_bytes([prefix[10], prefix[11], prefix[12], prefix[13]]);
899	    let dib_header_size = u32::from_le_bytes([prefix[14], prefix[15], prefix[16], prefix[17]]);
900	    if !(12..=124).contains(&dib_header_size) || pixel_offset < 14 + dib_header_size {
901	        return false;
902	    }
903	    // Colour planes then bit depth. BITMAPCOREHEADER declares u16 width and
904	    // height, every later header i32, which moves the pair from 22 to 26.
905	    let planes_at = if dib_header_size == 12 { 22 } else { 26 };
906	    let Some(f) = prefix.get(planes_at..planes_at + 4) else {
907	        return false;
908	    };
909	    u16::from_le_bytes([f[0], f[1]]) == 1
910	        && matches!(
911	            u16::from_le_bytes([f[2], f[3]]),
912	            // 0 is BI_JPEG / BI_PNG, where the DIB carries an embedded image.
913	            0 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32
914	        )
915	}

917	/// Adobe Photoshop: `8BPS` is followed by a big-endian version, 1 for PSD and
918	/// 2 for PSB. Nothing else is defined, so a text file whose first word is
919	/// `8BPS` fails here on its fifth byte.
920	fn psd_version(prefix: &[u8]) -> bool {
921	    prefix.len() >= 6 && prefix[4] == 0 && matches!(prefix[5], 1 | 2)

959	/// to appear as prose inside this PR's own target corpus, a Unity/3D-asset

984	/// minor version — immediately followed by an end-of-line marker, which the
985	/// spec requires right after the version (ISO 32000-1 §7.5.2, "the header
986	/// line shall be immediately followed by a comment... the header
987	/// itself... terminated by an end-of-line marker").
988	///
989	/// Unqualified, this signature is five ASCII characters including `%` and
990	/// `-`. Prose opening "%PDF- is the five byte header every PDF file begins
991	/// with. " sniffed `Family::Pdf` and was handed to the PDF extractor, which
992	/// cannot parse it (#403 — same class as #379/#380, filed separately: `%`
993	/// and `-` shrink the collision surface a lot, and the wrong answer is a
994	/// parse error rather than #379's silent junk reason). The qualifier is
995	/// exactly what makes it safe: a sentence has a space (or nothing) after
996	/// "1.7", never a CR/LF, and real generators always emit that break —
997	/// Adobe's own spec calls it out as required, not conventional.
998	fn pdf_header(prefix: &[u8]) -> bool {
999	    prefix.len() >= 9
1000	        && prefix[5].is_ascii_digit()
1001	        && prefix[6] == b'.'
1002	        && prefix[7].is_ascii_digit()
1003	        && matches!(prefix[8], b'\r' | b'\n')
1004	}

1006	/// Truevision TGA, which has no magic number at all — every byte of its
1007	/// 18-byte header is data. Detection is therefore by CONSTRAINT: an image type
1008	/// from the defined set, a pixel depth from the defined set, a colour-map
1009	/// descriptor that must be all-zero when there is no colour map, and non-zero
1010	/// dimensions.
1011	///
1012	/// The reason this is safe on text is byte 1 and byte 2: `color_map_type` is 0
1013	/// or 1 and `image_type` is one of six values below 12, so both the second and
1014	/// the third byte of the file have to be control characters. Prose, CSV, JSON
1015	/// and source code fail on byte 1.
1016	fn looks_like_tga_header(prefix: &[u8]) -> bool {
1017	    if prefix.len() < 18 {
1018	        return false;
1019	    }
1020	    let color_map_type = prefix[1];
1021	    if color_map_type > 1 {
1022	        return false;
1023	    }
1024	    // 1/2/3 uncompressed colour-mapped/true-colour/greyscale, 9/10/11 the
1025	    // run-length encoded counterparts. Type 0 ("no image data") is excluded
1026	    // deliberately: it carries no pixels, so nothing is lost by letting such a
1027	    // file fall through to the text heuristics, and admitting it would make an
1028	    // all-zero prefix a TGA.
1029	    if !matches!(prefix[2], 1 | 2 | 3 | 9 | 10 | 11) {
1030	        return false;
1031	    }
1032	    if !matches!(prefix[16], 8 | 15 | 16 | 24 | 32) {
1033	        return false;
1034	    }
1035	    if color_map_type == 0 && prefix[3..8].iter().any(|b| *b != 0) {
1036	        return false;
1037	    }
1038	    let width = u16::from_le_bytes([prefix[12], prefix[13]]);
1039	    let height = u16::from_le_bytes([prefix[14], prefix[15]]);
1040	    width > 0 && height > 0
1041	}

1043	/// POSIX/GNU tar: the `ustar` magic sits at offset 257 of the first 512-byte
1044	/// header block. Five printable letters are not evidence on their own (the
1045	/// `MAGIC_TABLE` invariant), so the header's own checksum has to agree: bytes
1046	/// 148..156 hold, in octal, the sum of all 512 header bytes with that field
1047	/// read as spaces. Text that happens to say `ustar` at byte 257 does not also
1048	/// carry a correct checksum of itself 109 bytes earlier.
1049	fn looks_like_tar_header(prefix: &[u8]) -> bool {
1050	    let Some(header) = prefix.get(..512) else {
1051	        return false;
1052	    };
1053	    if &header[257..262] != b"ustar" {
1054	        return false;
1055	    }
1056	    let stored = header[148..156]
1057	        .iter()
1058	        .skip_while(|b| **b == b' ')
1059	        .take_while(|b| (b'0'..=b'7').contains(*b))
1060	        .fold(0u64, |acc, b| acc * 8 + u64::from(*b - b'0'));

1062	        .iter()
1063	        .enumerate()
1064	        .map(|(i, b)| {
1065	            if (148..156).contains(&i) {
1066	                u64::from(b' ')
1067	            } else {
1068	                u64::from(*b)
1069	            }
1070	        })

1083	pub fn archive_advice(binary_kind: &str, gzip: bool) -> Option<String> {

1085	        ("zip", _) => ("zip archive", "unzip <file>"),
1086	        ("tar", true) => ("gzip-compressed tar archive", "tar -xzf <file>"),
1087	        ("tar", false) => ("tar archive", "tar -xf <file>"),
1088	        ("7z", _) => ("7z archive", "7z x <file>"),
1089	        ("rar", _) => ("rar archive", "unrar x <file>"),
1090	        ("xz", _) => (
1091	            "xz-compressed file",
1092	            "xz -dk <file>, or tar -xJf <file> for a .tar.xz",
1093	        ),
1094	        _ => return None,

1096	    Some(format!(
1097	        "unextracted {what}: autoindex does not open archives — extract it first ({how}), \

1128	    // key:value log. Gated on a STRONG header plus >=3 canonical headers so an
1129	    // ordinary `key: value` config or YAML never trips it.
1130	    // A mailbox is an email with a separator line in front of it, so it is
1131	    // tested first: the separator is not a header, and without this branch the
1132	    // `looks_like_email` gate below fails on line one and a multi-GB mailbox
1133	    // falls through to prose — every message's headers indexed as body text and
1134	    // the record cap cutting it off after the first few thousand sections.
1135	    if looks_like_mbox(nonblank) {
1136	        return Family::Mbox;
1137	    }
1138	    if looks_like_email(nonblank) {
1139	        return Family::Eml;
1140	    }

1143	    // file and — via the #551 frontmatter lookahead below — for a frontmatter
1144	    // body too.
1145	    if let Some(family) = classify_structured(text, nonblank) {
1146	        return family;

1150	    // frontmatter (Jekyll, Hugo, Obsidian, Docusaurus, MkDocs, Astro, and Claude
1151	    // Code skill files — including the two this repo ships). Without a lookahead
1152	    // for the *closing* `---` and what follows it, every such file was handed to
1153	    // the YAML extractor, which keeps the frontmatter mapping and the first
1154	    // paragraph and discards the rest of the body (#551, silent data loss). If
1155	    // the file opens with `---`, has a matching closing `---`, and the body after
1156	    // it is not itself YAML, classify by that body so the whole document is
1157	    // indexed. A pure/multi-document YAML file keeps YAML: the content after its
1158	    // `---` document marker is still YAML — judged on line shape first and, when

1254	        "cc",
1255	        "bcc",
1256	        "subject",
1257	        "date",
1258	        "message-id",
1259	        "received",
1260	        "return-path",
1261	        "reply-to",

1437	/// continuation lines: none of those lines are `key:`-shaped, so the body read
1438	/// as prose and the stream lost its per-document key structure. The
1439	/// discriminator that separates the two precisely is that
1440	/// markdown-with-frontmatter is *invalid* as a YAML stream — its body halts

1442	/// while a real multi-document stream parses.

1445	/// markdown paragraph decodes to, and any parse error both disqualify) and at

1447	/// Observed with serde_yaml 0.9: a markdown body yields `String` then `did not

1452	/// The parse runs on at most the 8 KiB sniff prefix, only for a body the line

1455	/// back into `Yaml` and undo #587 item 1 (measured: 341 files).
1456	///

1458	/// advance past a document that fails to parse, and this returns on the first
1459	/// error rather than continuing.
1460	///
1461	/// Residual, stated rather than hidden: a frontmatter body that is *literally*
1462	/// a YAML mapping written without `key:`-shaped lines (`Last updated: 2026-01-01`

1464	/// called YAML. It has to parse cleanly end to end for that, which no markdown
1465	/// containing a list, a table, a fenced block, an emphasis opener or two
1466	/// consecutive paragraphs does.

1468	    use serde::Deserialize as _;
1469	    let mut structured = 0usize;
1470	    for de in serde_yaml::Deserializer::from_str(text) {
1471	        match serde_yaml::Value::deserialize(de) {
1472	            Ok(serde_yaml::Value::Mapping(_) | serde_yaml::Value::Sequence(_)) => structured += 1,
1473	            // `---` on its own, or a comment-only document: carries no
1474	            // evidence either way.
1475	            Ok(serde_yaml::Value::Null) => {}
1476	            // A scalar document is what prose decodes to; an error means this
1477	            // is not a YAML stream at all.
1478	            Ok(_) | Err(_) => return false,
1479	        }
1480	    }
1481	    structured > 0
1482	}
